title: 선배님께서 핸드폰 보지 말라고  (You Told Me Not to Look at My Phone)

segments.t: Late at night in the KBS parking lot, Tak Ye-jin finally gets the scratched sedan's owner on the phone — and watches in disbelief as rookie Baek Seung-chan walks up to the car. Listen for the phrases for 'my father's car' and 'a repair estimate'.
근데 혹시 KBS 직원이세요?
세상에, 어머 그럼 같은 식구네요!
너는 왜 문자에 답을 안 하니?
선배님께서 핸드폰 보지 말라고 하셔가지고.
그냥 살짝 찍혔어.
예, 살짝이 아닌 것 같으세요.
이게 아버지 차다 보니까 일단 아버지께 말씀을 드리고요.
견적을 보고 추후에 연락을 드려야 할 것 같은데요.
Let's walk through the eight lines of this priceless parking-lot twist.
근데 혹시 KBS 직원이세요?

'By the way, do you happen to be a KBS employee?' Still on the phone before seeing who it is, Ye-jin pairs the word for 'by any chance' with the word for 'staff member' or 'employee', softened into a respectful question form The word doubles the.
세상에, 어머 그럼 같은 식구네요!

'Goodness, oh my, then we're part of the same family!' She opens with an exclamation that literally means 'in the world!' — a warm gasp like 'oh my goodness!'. Korean workplaces fondly call fellow coworkers a word meaning 'family members who share meals together' This short for that.
너는 왜 문자에 답을 안 하니?

'Why didn't you reply to my text messages?' The instant she sees it is rookie Seung-chan, all that honeyed politeness evaporates into the casual 'you'! She uses the everyday word for a text message and bluntly asks 'why don't you reply?' The word doubles the.
선배님께서 핸드폰 보지 말라고 하셔가지고.
'Because you told me not to look at my phone, senior.' Check and mate! Addressing her as his respected senior, Seung-chan quotes her own morning scolding — 'told me not to look' It is a handy word.
그냥 살짝 찍혔어.
'It just got a tiny nick.' Hoping to get off cheap, Ye-jin downplays the dent with a handy everyday word meaning 'lightly', 'barely', or 'just a tiny bit' The word doubles the.
예, 살짝이 아닌 것 같으세요.

'Yes, well, it doesn't look tiny.' Polite as ever on the surface, immovable underneath: Seung-chan echoes that exact same word right back to say 'it doesn't appear to be just a tiny scratch!' The word doubles the.
이게 아버지 차다 보니까 일단 아버지께 말씀을 드리고요.

'Since this is my father's car, I'll tell my father first.' He states that it is his father's car, using a connective ending that explains 'since that happens to be the case'. Notice how he upgrades 'speaking' to an honorific word for his dad It is a handy word.
견적을 보고 추후에 연락을 드려야 할 것 같은데요.

'I think I'll have to check the repair estimate and contact you later.' No easy pass for Ye-jin! He refers to an official repair quote from a body shop, and uses crisp, businesslike Korean for 'at a later date' The word doubles the. Now let's hear the whole nighttime parking-lot reveal again.
근데 혹시 KBS 직원이세요?
세상에, 어머 그럼 같은 식구네요!
너는 왜 문자에 답을 안 하니?
선배님께서 핸드폰 보지 말라고 하셔가지고.
그냥 살짝 찍혔어.
예, 살짝이 아닌 것 같으세요.
이게 아버지 차다 보니까 일단 아버지께 말씀을 드리고요.
견적을 보고 추후에 연락을 드려야 할 것 같은데요.
You picked up the words for employee, fellow colleagues, 'just a little', and a repair quote. Off to the writers' beef dinner next!
안녕히 가세요!
